About the Job

zerohash is looking for a Senior+ Software Engineer to architect and build our fiat payment systems, scaling our gateway to Finance 2.0. We are a high-performing team looking for an equally ambitious and driven teammate. The right candidate for this position is detail-oriented, deeply technical, and driven by the challenges of complex financial systems. You are eager to build secure, resilient, and highly scalable banking infrastructure. If you are looking to have a massive impact in a high-growth startup bridging the gap between traditional finance and digital assets, you will find this role uniquely challenging and rewarding.

Role Objectives & Focus

This senior-level role focuses intensely on the backbone of our financial infrastructure:

  • Fiat Payments: Building and maintaining robust fiat rails such as ACH, RTP, FedNow, RFP in the US, and SEPA in Europe.
  • Banking Infrastructure: Direct API integrations with top-tier banking partners.
  • Treasury Management: Developing sophisticated software to autonomously manage and reconcile balances across banking networks.
  • Operational Tooling: Creating internal tooling to streamline financial operations and scale our capacity to handle millions of transactions securely.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the architectural design and hands-on development of our global fiat payment rails (ACH, RTP, FedNow, Request for Pay, and SEPA).
  • Architect, implement, and scale seamless API integrations into our banking partners' systems.
  • Design and build robust treasury management software for internal operations, allowing programmatic liquidity management and automated balance transfers between partner banks.
  • Develop robust internal operational tooling to support reconciliation, automated alerts, financial operations, and compliance reporting.
  • Support the company's vital business by contributing to the design and development of software in an event-driven microservices environment.
  • Develop microservices, primarily utilizing Golang.
  • Work closely with platform engineers to set up new services and scale existing infrastructure.
  • Respond to production issues and alerts, ensuring high availability of our payment gateways.
  • When necessary, communicate directly with banking partners and client technical teams to resolve complex integration issues.

Requirements

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience, specifically focused on Payments, FinTech, or Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) infrastructure.
  • Deep proficiency with Golang in a production environment.
  • Extensive understanding of traditional fiat networks and clearing systems (e.g., ACH, RTP, FedNow, SEPA, Swift).
  • Strong expertise in SQL and complex database schema design for high-throughput, ACID-compliant financial ledgers.
  • Hands-on experience developing, integrating, and maintaining resilient connections with bank APIs and third-party payment processors.
  • A humble and scrappy get-it-done mindset; you're resourceful and in your element going from 0 to 1.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills; you can systematically troubleshoot complex distributed systems.
  • Comfort with ambiguity; the ability to independently lay out and test clear hypotheses, and solve architectural problems without well-defined direction.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelors in Computer Science or equivalent experience.
  • Experience at a banking-as-a-service, brokerage-as-a-service, or payment-as-a-service business.
  • Proven track record of building treasury management or automated ledgering systems from scratch.
  • Experience with digital assets and crypto infrastructure.
  • Experience with distributed systems design and messaging frameworks (e.g., Kafka, ZeroMQ, or NATS) for data distribution and persistence.

Benefits

  • Healthcare Insurance: zerohash covers roughly 100% of employee premiums as well as a portion of spouse/children (U.S. only)
  • Vision & Dental Insurance (U.S. only)
  • Chance to earn equity
  • Maternity & Paternity leave (after 6 months)
  • WeWork All Access Membership
  • WFH Yearly Stipend
  • L&D Yearly Stipend (after 6 months)

About zerohash

zerohash is the leading crypto and stablecoin infrastructure platform and the operating system for digital money, powering the next generation of financial services. Founded in 2017, zerohash enables banks, brokerages, fintechs, and payment companies to offer crypto trading, stablecoin payments, and tokenized assets without having to build or manage complex blockchain infrastructure on their own.

The zerohash platform supports three core pillars: Trade, Transact, and Tokenize. Through a single integration, customers can launch regulated crypto buy, sell, and custody services; enable 24/7 stablecoin-based funding, payouts, and settlement; and issue and manage tokenized assets with built-in compliance, risk controls, and reporting. By abstracting away technical, regulatory, and operational complexity, zerohash allows partners to treat digital assets as just another financial primitive: fast, programmable, and global.

zerohash is trusted by some of the world’s most recognized financial and consumer brands, including Interactive Brokers, Morgan Stanley, Stripe, Franklin Templeton, BlackRock, DraftKings, Gusto, Worldpay, Kalshi, One Pay, among others. Today, zerohash infrastructure supports millions of end users across brokerage, wealth, payments, and marketplace platforms globally.

The company is deeply regulated and compliance-first, operating across the U.S. and internationally with licenses and approvals that allow partners to enter crypto and stablecoins with confidence. zerohash has become a trusted partner for enterprises seeking to modernize financial products while meeting the highest standards for security, risk management, and regulatory oversight.

To date, zerohash has raised over $280 million in funding from a mix of leading venture firms and strategic investors, including Morgan Stanley, Interactive Brokers, SoFi, Point72 Ventures, Bain Capital Crypto, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and more.

zerohash has been featured in top-tier media outlets such as Bloomberg, CNBC, The Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, Reuters, Forbes, and CoinDesk, and its leadership team regularly contributes to global conversations on the future of payments, investing, and financial infrastructure.

At zerohash, we're building the infrastructure that makes digital money work securely, compliantly, and at global scale.

The zerohash Culture

All zerohash employees are guided by the following characteristics and core principles:

  • Independence/Ownership - An ability to work autonomously. Join zerohash, pitch ideas, and shape the work you do.
  • Passion - We are innovating quickly and challenging the status quo. We want you to think big, be creative and ​make a difference every day.
  • Collaborative - A good attitude and respect for others. We’re teammates, not co-workers. Everything we do is a shared success and equally a shared failure - we talk in terms of “we” not “me”.
  • Initiative - An ability and passion for learning and asking questions. We will champion you, challenge you and push you to achieve your best - and we expect you to do the same.
  • Empathy - An ability to listen, respect, and understand your co-workers, customers, and everyone you interact with no matter how different they are to you.
  • Adaptability - An ability to respond quickly. We are in a fast-paced industry and so we expect you to be creative when solving a new problem and comfortable under pressure.
  • Transparency - We believe that transparency is critical to empowering everyone to make the best decisions, both the company to its people and vice versa.
  • Integrity - Integrity creates trust. As both an organization collectively and as individuals, it is our most valuable asset.

Who we are:

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.

Our culture:

  • We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.

  • We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

  • We're a remote-first team spread across time zones, so no office to report to - work from wherever helps you do your best work. Just a couple of things to keep in mind: pay is based on where you're located, and you'll need to keep a home base in the country you're hired in. So while we love the "coffee shop today, mountains tomorrow" life, this isn't a passport-optional, work-from-anywhere-on-Earth kind of remote - think flexible within your country, not borderless.

Location:

  • Remote - US / Canada

About the role:

Fraud has moved to mobile, and so have the tools fraudsters use: emulators, rooted and jailbroken devices, hooking frameworks, app repackaging, and device farms. Sardine's Device Intelligence & Behavior Biometrics team builds the signals that tell genuine users apart from fraudsters, bots, and automated or manipulated devices, and our iOS and Android SDKs run inside the apps of fintechs and enterprises worldwide.

We are looking for a Mobile SDK Engineer to strengthen our mobile fraud prevention capabilities. You will develop new device, integrity, and behavioral signals for our native iOS and Android SDKs, keep device identity stable across reinstalls and OS changes, and make the SDKs fast, lightweight, and easy for customers to integrate.

What you'll be doing:

  • Design, develop, and maintain our native iOS and Android SDKs, keeping them lightweight, stable, and easy to integrate.

  • Research and implement new fraud signals: emulator and virtual device detection, root and jailbreak detection, hooking and instrumentation detection (for example Frida), app tampering and repackaging, remote access and screen sharing, and device farm patterns.

  • Improve device identity longevity across app reinstalls, OS upgrades, and platform privacy changes, using platform capabilities such as Keychain, App Attest / DeviceCheck, and Play Integrity where appropriate.

  • Collect sensor, touch, and interaction data that powers our behavior biometrics, with careful attention to battery, performance, and privacy.

  • Harden the SDKs against reverse engineering, tampering, and spoofed payloads.

  • Work with the Web SDK and backend (Go) teams on cross-platform features, such as linking native app sessions to in-app WebView sessions.

  • Test thoroughly across devices, OS versions, and integration setups to ensure compatibility, reliability, and stability.

  • Track iOS and Android platform changes ahead of release and adapt the SDKs before they affect customers.

  • Support customer developers during integration and troubleshoot issues in their apps.

  • Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and knowledge sharing with a distributed team.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience building native Android and / or iOS apps or SDKs.

  • Strong Android (Kotlin / Java) and / or iOS (Swift / Objective-C) fundamentals, and willingness to dive into lower-level concepts such as memory management, threading, and the platform runtime.

  • Solid grasp of mobile security concepts: sandboxing, code signing, entitlements and permissions, root and jailbreak behavior, and emulator characteristics.

  • Experience with reverse engineering, dynamic instrumentation, or similar investigative work on mobile apps.

  • Experience shipping a library or SDK that other developers integrate, with attention to API design, binary size, and backward compatibility.

  • Experience with mobile testing frameworks such as XCTest / Xcode UI Testing and Espresso.

  • Strong understanding of object-oriented programming principles and design patterns.

  • Clear written and verbal communication.

  • Understanding of how AI is used by fraudsters (automated tampering, hooking frameworks, emulators, synthetic devices) and how that shapes SDK defense and signal design.

  • Experience using AI to speed up investigation work: reading crash logs, analyzing device signal data, or comparing behavior across OS versions.

Nice to Have

  • Background in mobile fraud prevention, security, or device intelligence.

  • Hands-on experience with Frida, Objection, LLDB, jadx, Ghidra, or similar tools.

  • Native code experience (C / C++ via NDK, or low-level iOS runtime).

  • Experience with cross-platform wrappers that customers use to integrate SDKs, such as React Native, Flutter, Expo, or Xamarin.

  • Experience writing backend services in Go, Java, C++, or Rust.

  • Experience with GCP.

  • Understanding of behavioral biometrics.

  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and release automation, using tools such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins, to automate the building, testing, versioning, and deployment of SDKs or applications

Tech Stack

  • iOS SDK: Swift / Objective-C

  • Android SDK: Kotlin / Java

  • Backend: Go

  • Infrastructure: GCP / AWS

Benefits we offer:

  • Generous compensation in cash and equity

  • Early exercise for all options, including pre-vested

  • Work from anywhere: Remote-first Culture

  • Flexible paid time off and Year-end break

  • Health insurance, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents - US and Canada specific

  • 4% matching in 401k / RRSP - US and Canada specific

  • MacBook Pro delivered to your door

  • One-time stipend to set up a home office — desk, chair, screen, etc.

  • Monthly meal stipend

  • Monthly social meet-up stipend

  • Annual health and wellness stipend

  • Annual Learning stipend

Join a fast-growing company with world-class professionals from around the world. If you are seeking a meaningful career, you found the right place, and we would love to hear from you.

To learn more about how we process your personal information and your rights in regards to your personal information as an applicant and Sardine employee, please visit our Applicant and Worker Privacy Notice.

descriptions.job-16r5t8v:
About us

Relay is a cross-chain payments protocol that provides instant, low-cost cross-chain bridging, swaps, and transactions. We're the fastest and cheapest way to bridge and transact across chains, serving over 5 million users who have completed 59+ million transactions with $6+ billion in volume across 85+ chains.

Our company mission is to make transacting across chains as fast, cheap, and reliable as online payments. We are building the core infrastructure to abstract chains from end user payments, enabling the next billion users to experience the benefits of blockchain without the UX burdens.

About the role

The Liquidity team keeps Relay's liquidity reliable, competitively priced, capital-efficient, and within its risk framework. Our engineers build the systems that hold and move Relay's inventory across chains, wallets, exchanges and bridges. We are now building the foundations that let liquidity scale with our partner deals, and we are hiring senior engineers to own them.

We are hiring for three areas, and we will agree yours with you before the offer, based on your background:

  • Reference data: one source of truth for assets, chains, contracts, venues and limits, with a safe change process, so new assets and chains go live through configuration rather than code.

  • Ledger and P&L: positions and P&L across chains, wallets, exchanges, bridges and in-flight transfers, reconciled daily.

  • Protocol liquidity: protocol-level liquidity in on-chain pools, and the design of a liquidity layer with our Protocol team.

You will design, build and run your area in production, and take turns on the team's support rotation, where you help onboard partner deals and new chains and investigate incidents.

We work agentic-first: AI agents extend how much we can design, build and verify, while people remain accountable for decisions that move capital or change production behavior.

What you'll do

Build and own your area

  • Design, build and run the systems for your area, from the first design document to production and on-call.

  • Write tests, monitoring and runbooks for everything you ship.

  • Measure the outcome: assets onboarded without code changes, balances reconciled, or liquidity deployed within limits.

Give operations safe controls

  • Replace database edits and code changes with configuration that has validation, approvals, an audit trail and rollback.

  • Work with our operations engineers and trading desk lead on the controls they use every day.

Work across the team

  • Implement pricing, hedging and rebalancing models with our quant developers.

  • Take part in design reviews with the tech lead and the principal engineer.

  • Join the support rotation: deal and chain onboarding, incident investigation and fixes.

About you

  • You've built systems that handle money, and you care that every number matches.

  • You own what you ship in production, including monitoring and on-call.

  • You write a short design before you build, and you ship in small, safe steps.

  • You like working with operations and quant teammates, and you build tools they can use without you.

  • You use AI agents to write, test and review code, and you validate what they produce.

  • You're excited about crypto and cross-chain liquidity.

Skills and abilities

Must-have

  • 5+ years of backend engineering on production systems that handle money or financial data.

  • Strong TypeScript/Node.js or another backend language, and SQL (Postgres).

  • Experience with correctness in data-heavy systems: idempotency, consistency, reconciliation, schema design and migrations.

  • Depth in at least one of: ledgers or accounting systems; reference or master data; DeFi protocols, AMMs and smart contracts.

  • Production ownership: monitoring, on-call and incident follow-up.

Nice to have

  • EVM or Solana development, bridges, exchange APIs, AMMs such as Curve or Uniswap, Solidity.

  • Trading, exchange, payments or fintech back-office experience.

  • Market or reference data at a trading firm or data vendor.

  • Python for data work.

Location and hours

  • Remote, with at least three hours of overlap with 08:00–17:00 UTC. We especially welcome candidates in Latin America and Europe.

  • Our engineers take turns on a support rotation that can require access to global exchanges whose eligibility rules exclude some jurisdictions, including the United States and Canada. We can only consider candidates located outside those jurisdictions.

What we offer

  • Competitive base salary

  • Equity package

  • Comprehensive health benefits

  • Unlimited PTO policy with encouraged minimum

  • Remote-first culture with emphasis on collaboration, communication, and flexibility

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

We’re looking for a Senior Recruiting Coordinator to deliver an exceptional candidate and interviewer experience and help lead the day-to-day work of our global coordination team. You’ll own complex interview scheduling, bring deep Ashby expertise, use metrics to improve performance, and mentor fellow coordinators. You’ll also manage the day-to-day work of the AI agents we’re building to support recruiting coordination.

Partnering closely with Talent Operations, you’ll improve how our people, systems, and AI agents work together. This is a hands-on role for someone who communicates proactively, brings solutions, and moves with urgency, with opportunities to grow into people management over time.

The impact you will have:

  • Own complex interview scheduling across teams and time zones, delivering a responsive, well-organized experience for candidates and interviewers.

  • Serve as the team’s Ashby expert, resolving scheduling issues, coaching coordinators, and partnering with Talent Operations to improve workflows.

  • Own day-to-day coordination operations and support Talent Operations projects, keeping Ashby records, interview plans, and scheduling data accurate and up to date.

  • Drive coordination performance through accurate reporting on interview volume, time to schedule, SLA adherence, reschedules, and candidate and interviewer feedback.

  • Develop fellow coordinators through onboarding, training, and practical coaching, helping the team manage priorities, workloads, and coverage.

  • Manage AI agents that support recruiting coordination, reviewing their work, resolving exceptions, and improving their accuracy and reliability with Talent Operations.

  • Partner closely with recruiters and the Talent team, aligning on priorities, communicating risks early, and bringing clear recommendations that keep interviews moving.

What we’re looking for:

  • 4+ years of recruiting coordination experience, with demonstrated success managing complex, high-volume scheduling in a fast-moving environment.

  • Advanced Ashby expertise is required, including interview plans, interviewer pools, scheduling links, calendar integrations, and independent troubleshooting.

  • Experience supporting Talent Operations or coordination operations, including ATS data quality, workflow maintenance, and process documentation.

  • Strong command of Ashby reporting and coordination metrics, with a track record of translating data into better scheduling outcomes.

  • Experience mentoring coordinators, leading training, and helping teammates use Ashby confidently and effectively.

  • Clear, proactive communication and the ability to build trusted partnerships with candidates, interviewers, recruiters, and Talent Operations.

  • Sound judgment and a strong sense of urgency: you investigate problems, recommend solutions, and follow through without repeated direction.

  • Applied AI fluency, including writing instructions, evaluating outputs, and identifying when human judgment is needed. Experience managing AI agents is a strong plus.

About the Team:

  • Our talent team is fully remote, embracing async communication and collaboration through Slack channels, thorough documentation, and proactive updates to keep work moving forward smoothly across time zones.

  • We hold weekly RC team syncs to review priorities and solve coordination challenges. Coordinators also participate in hiring syncs for the roles they support, staying close to candidate progress, hiring decisions, and upcoming needs.

  • Driven by a dedication to our craft, we continuously refine our best practices and data quality to deliver an exceptional experience for both internal stakeholders and candidates, supported by precise, reliable reporting.

Team Operating Rhythms:

  • Based in the Pacific Time Zone, working 8:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m. PT.

  • As a globally distributed team, we operate across various time zones, yet most of us overlap for collaboration and meetings between 7 a.m.–12 p.m. PT.

  • An active scheduling workload alongside coordination operations, Ashby data maintenance, mentoring, reporting, and AI agent oversight.

  • Advance coverage planning for holidays and absences, with clear owners and next steps.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • When an interviewer cancels, you promptly identify alternatives, recommend a solution, and confirm the revised plan with the candidate and interview team.

  • When scheduling misses turnaround targets, you use Ashby data to diagnose the issue, recommend a change, and track whether performance improves.

  • When an AI agent sends incomplete instructions, you correct the affected communications and partner with Talent Operations to test a fix.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com.

Recruitment agencies

About Arca

Arca is a wealth management firm built from the ground up with AI. Most people get financial advice that's reactive: an annual check-in, a plan that's a document instead of a living thing, a relationship where you're one of three hundred clients your advisor is trying to remember. We think that's backwards. The kind of service that used to require a team of specialists behind you, the kind that makes you feel like the only person in the room, should be available to far more than the ultra-wealthy.

So we're building it. We're not SaaS — we are the wealth management business, rebuilding it from the inside with AI. Our platform is an Iron Man suit for advisors: it takes over the low-leverage work so they can focus on what actually requires a human, showing up with empathy, context, and judgment. Underneath, it keeps a living understanding of each client. It remembers the thing you mentioned once, six months ago. It notices when your life changes — a new job, a new kid, a market shift — and adjusts before you think to ask. You won't see the technology. You'll just notice your advisor seems to know you better than any financial professional ever has.

That's the product we're growing: client by client, on the strength of the experience itself. We started by acquiring firms managing over $1B in client assets, which gave us real advisors, real clients, and real financial outcomes to build against from day one. But acquisition was the starting line. The bet is that an advisor backed by this platform delivers something good enough that clients come to us on their own.

It's a $20T market, and we think it's ready to be rebuilt.

— Rron, CEO

 

The receipts

  • Stage: Series A, $64M raised

  • Backed by: General Catalyst, Index Ventures, Venrock

  • Board & Advisors: Former CEO of Vanguard, Former CFO of Schwab, Founder of Altruist, Morgan Housel (author of The Psychology of Money), Will Guidara (former co-owner of Eleven Madison Park and author of Unreasonable Hospitality)

 

The team

We’re small on purpose and engineering heavy: about 80% of the team is technical. We’re based in NYC and hail from high growth startups like Stripe, Ramp, Rippling, Plaid, Doordash, and Glean.

We’re fully in-office in Flatiron, five days a week—lunch together, coffee breaks, basketball games, happy hours.

 

The role

As Arca's Head of Tax, you'll build our tax practice from zero — the first tax hire, with a blank page and a mandate to make tax a proactive part of clients' financial life. Tax is where most of our clients feel the most friction, feel the most uncertain, and get the least help. A scramble for documents every spring, a preparer who sees one year at a time, and a wealth advisor who's never quite looped in. We think tax should be continuous, coordinated with the rest of the plan, and done ahead of the deadline instead of after it.

You're here to build an AI-native tax practice from day one including the document gathering process, return preparation and review, client projection/planning before a client thinks to ask, and more. You'll design what the agents do, where a professional's judgment has to step in, and ensure end-to-end quality.

This is a hands-on role involving return preparation, directly helping clients on their most complex situations, partner closely with our wealth advisors so tax and investment advice move as one, and own the service as a business: pricing, revenue, capacity, and the team you'll hire behind you. Most of your time goes to two things: doing the tax work and designing the platform that does it better, sitting next to the engineers who build it.

 

What you’ll own

  • The tax practice. What we offer — starting with individual returns (1040s) and year-round planning, projections, and notices, and expanding to business returns (S-corps and other entity returns) for clients who own businesses — who it's for, and the standard every engagement is held to. You set the scope, the service model, the quality bar as well as selecting vendors (core tax return software in particular) to enable the business.

  • An AI-native tax process. End-to-end design of how tax work gets done at Arca — document collection, data normalization, preparation, review, filing, and post-filing. You'll work side by side with engineering and product to build it, and be the domain authority on every workflow.

  • Clients. You prepare, review, and own returns for clients whose situations take real expertise: stock options and RSUs, business income, S-corp owners, rental real estate, and multi-state filings. You explain tax in plain English and give clients confidence their needs are handled.

  • Partnership with our wealth advisors. Tax and investment advice as one plan, not two silos. You work with advisors on tax-loss harvesting, Roth conversions, charitable strategy, equity comp exercise timing, and withholding and estimated payments — and build the playbooks so advisors know when to bring you in.

  • Risk, compliance, and quality. Preparer standards, Circular 230 obligations, data security, engagement letters, review protocols, and an audit trail for every AI-assisted step.

  • The team. Hiring the preparers, reviewers, and specialists who come after you, and deciding which work we keep in-house versus partner on.

 

Example problems you’d work on

These are the kinds of questions the first year of this practice has to answer.

  • Tax season without the scramble. We already manage client accounts and know most of their financial picture. What does it take to have 80% of a return assembled before a client uploads a single document — and how do agents chase the remaining 20% seamlessly?

  • Where the agent stops and the professional starts. An agent can reconcile a 1099-B in seconds. It probably shouldn't be the one deciding how to treat a messy ISO disqualifying disposition. Drawing that line, and building a review layer that makes AI-prepared work more reliable than the traditional kind, is the core design problem.

  • Tax as a year-round signal. A client gets a bonus, sells a rental, or exercises options in July. How does the platform notice, rerun the projection, and get the right recommendation in front of the advisor while there's still time to act?

  • One plan, two disciplines. Every rebalance has a tax consequence, and every tax decision changes the investment plan. Designing how tax and wealth advice move together, inside one system, is what makes the model work.

 

The kind of person who thrives here

You’re excited by ownership, ambiguity, and building things that matter.

  • You're a licensed tax professional. Active CPA license required, with 8–15+ years in individual and high-net-worth tax experience at a top firm, family office, or planning-focused practice. You've prepared and reviewed complex 1040s yourself and signed off on others' work. Equity compensation, rental real estate, and multi-state are familiar ground, and you're comfortable with the business returns that come with owner-clients: S-corps, partnerships, and C-corps.

  • You're a change agent. You've stood up a practice, introduced a new service line, or materially improved ways of operating. You take initiative, operate independently, and have driven impact and results.

  • You're AI-pilled. You already use AI in your work and have strong opinions on which parts of the tax process it should own. You don't need to write code; you need to know exactly what's slow, what's error-prone, and what a great system would do instead — and enjoy working next to the engineers who build it.

  • Clients and advisors trust you. You can sit with a client and make a complicated situation feel simple, and you see wealth advisors as partners. Experience working alongside a wealth management or RIA practice is a big plus.

  • You hold a high bar because of what's at stake. This is people's money, their filings, and their standing with the IRS. "Good enough" means something different when a mistake shows up as a notice in someone's mailbox.

  • You're someone people actually want to be in the room with. This is a small team, one office, five days a week, working on problems that don't have clean answers. Kind, direct, and low-ego, you can give candid feedback without being a jerk, and you're genuinely energized by this environment.

 

Why now is the moment to join

This is a narrow window with unusually high leverage.

  • You're the first. No legacy process, no inherited tools, no one else's practice to fix. Whoever takes this on defines tax at Arca.

  • The clients are already here. We have real advisors and over $1B in client assets on the platform, and more firms and advisors joining. You're building a practice with demand on day one.

  • The platform is live. Agents already do real work for our advisors. You get to extend a working system into tax rather than wait for one to be built.

  • Tax is the next chapter. As Arca expands from wealth management into tax, estate planning, insurance, and beyond, tax is the first step. The patterns you set become the template for every service line after it.

Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k), and more.

Your Role:

As the Crypto Compliance Analyst, you’ll work directly with the Chief Compliance Officer of Alpaca Crypto LLC to run the day-to-day AML, sanctions and financial crimes program for our digital asset platform. You’ll investigate activity across both fiat rails and public blockchains. That means tracing funds through wallets, exchanges, bridges and DeFi protocols to catch illicit finance risk before it reaches our platform or our partners.

This role suits someone fluent in both blockchain forensics and BSA/AML fundamentals. You’ll help scale crypto compliance controls across an API-first platform that serves fintechs, brokers and their end users around the world.

Key Responsibilities:

  • On-Chain Transaction Monitoring: Review and disposition fiat and crypto transaction monitoring alerts every day, including deposit and withdrawal wallet screening, exposure-based alerts and behavioral red flags. Typical examples are rapid in-and-out flows, structuring across addresses and peel chains.
  • Blockchain Investigations: Run deep-dive investigations that trace funds across multiple hops, chains and asset types. Work through cross-chain bridges, swaps, mixers and other obfuscation methods, and attribute counterparties such as VASPs, DeFi protocols, self-hosted wallets and high-risk services.
  • Typology Detection: Identify and escalate activity tied to crypto-specific typologies. These include darknet markets, ransomware, scams and pig-butchering schemes, sanctioned entities, fraud shops, address poisoning, stolen funds and terrorist financing.
  • Sanctions and Wallet Screening: Screen customers, counterparties and wallet addresses against OFAC and other sanctions lists, including SDN-listed digital currency addresses. Investigate direct and indirect exposure to sanctioned or blocked parties and escalate potential matches.
  • Travel Rule and Counterparty Due Diligence: Support Travel Rule compliance for crypto transfers. Conduct due diligence on counterparty VASPs and assess the risk of transfers to and from unhosted wallets.
  • KYC/KYB and EDD: Handle escalated KYC/KYB reviews and Enhanced Due Diligence on high-risk customers and partners. This includes source-of-funds and source-of-wealth analysis that draws on on-chain history.
  • Rule Tuning and Risk Calibration: Work with the CCO and compliance engineering to tune monitoring rules, blockchain analytics risk scores and exposure thresholds. The goal is to cut false positives while keeping pace with new typologies, assets and chains.
  • Regulatory and Threat Intelligence: Track crypto-specific regulatory developments, including FinCEN virtual currency guidance, FATF guidance on virtual assets and VASPs, state money transmission requirements, and new stablecoin regulation such as the GENIUS Act. Also follow emerging illicit finance trends, and turn what you learn into updated procedures and controls.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Work with customer support, engineering and product to build compliance controls into the Alpaca API ecosystem. Weigh in on compliance risk when new assets, networks or features launch.

What You Need:

  • Experience: 2–5+ years in AML, transaction monitoring or financial crimes compliance. At least part of that should be at a crypto exchange, custodian, crypto-native fintech or blockchain analytics firm.
  • Blockchain Forensics: Hands-on experience tracing funds with tools such as Chainalysis (Reactor/KYT), TRM Labs or Elliptic. You’re comfortable reading block explorers (e.g., Etherscan) and interpreting transaction-level data.
  • Crypto Fluency: A solid working knowledge of how major networks work (Bitcoin’s UTXO model, Ethereum and EVM chains, Solana and others). You also understand stablecoins, smart contracts, DeFi protocols, bridges, and how illicit actors exploit each of them.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: A good grasp of BSA/AML obligations for money services businesses, OFAC sanctions (including digital currency address designations), FinCEN guidance on convertible virtual currency, the Travel Rule, and FATF standards for VASPs.
  • Investigative Writing: You can turn complex on-chain and off-chain evidence into concise, well-supported narratives for SARs, escalations and audit or exam requests.
  • Tools: Experience with blockchain analytics platforms, traditional fiat transaction monitoring and case management systems, and ideally Travel Rule solutions.
  • Autonomy: You’re self-directed, comfortable with ambiguity, and work well in a fast-paced, fully remote startup.
  • Bonus:
    • Certifications such as CAMS, CGSS, CCAS, or vendor certifications like Chainalysis Reactor Certification (CRC) or Chainalysis Investigations Specialist (CICS).
    • Experience supporting regulatory exams or independent AML audits for a crypto business.
    • Familiarity with data analysis 
    • Experience with B2B2C or API-driven platforms, including partner/nested account risk.

  • Health Benefits
  • New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500

When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. 

Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods.
